''Medicago tenderiensis'' Klokov }} '''''Medicago falcata''''' is a plant species of the genus ''[[Medicago]]''. It is native to much of Europe and Asia,{{Cite web|url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:506175-1|title=Medicago falcata L. | Plants of the World Online | Kew Science}} but is found throughout the world. It forms a [[symbiosis|symbiotic]] relationship with the bacterium ''[[Sinorhizobium meliloti]]'', which is capable of [[nitrogen fixation]]. Its common names include '''yellow lucerne''', '''sickle alfalfa''', '''yellow-flowered alfalfa''', '''yellow alfalfa''', '''sickle medick''' and '''yellow medick'''. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== * [https://www.ildis.org/LegumeWeb/6.00/taxa/5786.shtml International Legume Database & Information Services] {{Taxonbar|from=Q158531}} [[Category:Medicago|falcata]] [[Category:Plants described in 1753]] [[Category:Botanical taxa named by Carl Linnaeus]] [[Category:Flora of Lebanon and Syria]] {{Trifolieae-stub}}
